ranking.rationale: Owns the gravity-driven two-stable-pose reveal and compact support-free rocking motion.
Strong negative-space and silhouette instincts, but the defining action is a physical rock rather than projected light.
Strong readable occluders, but shadow projection is not the product interaction.
Strong compact transformation craft, though no folding or multi-part puzzle is wanted.
Transformation focus is relevant, but deployable mechanisms would compromise the one-piece talisman.
Kinetic-machine reasoning helps, though the restrained gravity cam is smaller and quieter than Bob's usual machines.
Captive-motion rigor is useful, but no captive element is needed.
Negative-space pattern skill is adjacent, but modular arrangement is absent.
Character-world sensibility helps the dragon, but does not own the rocker reveal.
Truthful physical demonstration is useful, but this is poetic transformation rather than a science object.
Passive interaction fits, but acoustics are not part of the Wish.
Abstract-game clarity is useful but there are no rules or opponent decisions.
Printable-game craft is not central to a talisman without gameplay.
Known-classic personalization is least relevant to an original kinetic silhouette object.
